The must-sees

  • Birgu

    Neighbourhood

    The Knights made it their first base when they arrived in 1530. After the Great Siege of 1565 it was given the title Città Vittoriosa, the victorious city.

    Look for: Find the Inquisitor’s Palace, where the Roman Inquisition in Malta held court and kept prisoners from 1574 until 1798.

  • Fort St Angelo

    Fortress

    It was the headquarters of the Knights during the Great Siege of 1565. Under British rule it was a Royal Navy base, and part of it is still used by the Order of Malta.

  • Fort St Elmo

    Fortress

    During the Great Siege of 1565 its small garrison held out for about a month before it fell to the Ottomans. It now houses the National War Museum, where Malta’s George Cross is displayed.

    Look for: In the war museum, find Faith, the battered biplane fighter that helped defend Malta’s skies in 1940.

  • Grandmaster’s Palace

    Palace

    It was the seat of the Grand Masters of the Order of St John, then of British governors. Today it houses the Office of the President of Malta and the Palace Armoury.

    Look for: In Prince Alfred’s Courtyard, an 18th-century clock has bronze figures of Moors that strike the hours on its bells.

  • St John’s Co-Cathedral

    Church · 1577

    Girolamo Cassar built it for the Knights of St John, and it was finished in 1577. Caravaggio’s Beheading of Saint John the Baptist, the only painting he signed, hangs in its oratory.

    Look for: The floor is a patchwork of about 400 inlaid marble tombstones of knights, with skulls, coats of arms and Latin epitaphs.

  • Upper Barrakka Gardens

    Viewpoint

    The gardens were laid out in the 17th century for the Italian knights of the Order. On the terrace below, the cannons of the Saluting Battery are fired every day at noon.

    Look for: Lean over the parapet for the Three Cities across the water; to one side, a lift drops down the face of the bastion to the harbour.

How it works

  1. Open Wizzy in Valletta and tap Start walk, or pick a ready-made walk.
  2. Put your phone in your pocket. Wizzy runs in the background, even with the screen locked.
  3. When you pass a place, you get a ping. Open it for the story, or keep walking.

Every place you see gets stamped in your Valletta passport. Your location stays on your phone. No ads, no tracking.
